 The same thematic material is also cross-referenced against non-Pali parallels, including the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 306–326), the Sanskrit and Tibetan *Udānavarga* (UV 28; Uv Kg 28), and Chinese canonical versions (T 210.20 and T 212.29).

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal text reuse with other debates in the *Kathāvatthu*, identifying 214 matching passages shared across 12 Pali texts, but no external cross-language matches reaching the reporting threshold [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial textual overlap occurs with the closely paired *Niggahakathā* (Kv 16.1), comprising 62 matches and a shared sequence spanning §1.15–9.8 of this text and §1.4–0.3 of Kv 16.1 [DharmaNexus]. Other significant internal reuse occurs with the *Vimuttikathā* (Kv 3.3; 42 matches), the *Sukhānuppadānakathā* (Kv 16.3; 18 matches), the *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1; 21 matches), and the *Paravitāraṇakathā* (Kv 2.4; 18 matches) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
